stem: A manufacturing company needs Rs 75000 in 3 years to overhaul its plant. It deposits equal amounts at the end of each half-year into a fund earning 10% per annum compounded half-yearly. What is each half-yearly deposit? [Given: (1.05)^6 = 1.3401, so the FV annuity factor = (1.3401 - 1) / 0.05 = 6.802]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Half-yearly rate = 5%, n = 6 half-year periods. R = 75000 / 6.802 = Rs 11026 (approx).
Ignoring interest, using 6 equal deposits: 75000 / 6 = Rs 12500.
Using annual rate 10% and 3 periods instead of the correct half-yearly setup: 75000 / [(1.10)^3-1]/0.10 = 75000/3.31 = ... but using a factor of 7.0 by mistake: 75000/7.0 = 10714 approx.
Using only 3 periods (one per year) instead of 6: FV factor using 3 periods at 5% = (1.1576-1)/0.05 = 3.152; 75000/5.5 = 13636 approx.

explanation: Convert to half-yearly: rate = 10%/2 = 5%, periods = 3*2 = 6. FV annuity factor = (1.3401-1)/0.05 = 6.802. R = 75000/6.802 = Rs 11026 (approx).

explanation_sections.punchline: The rate-period conversion to half-yearly is the decisive step before applying the sinking fund formula.
explanation_sections.approach: Name the formula: R = FV / [(1+i)^m - 1)/i] where i = 10%/2 = 5% and m = 3*2 = 6. From hint FVAF = 6.802. R = 75000 / 6.802 = 11026.
explanation_sections.lesson: For deposits more frequent than annual, always convert both rate and periods to match the deposit frequency.
explanation_sections.timing: 70-80 seconds. Key step: recognise 3 years with half-yearly deposits = 6 periods at 5%.
